concerns.text: SC-001 lacks a quantitative pass/fail threshold – it only states that MAE will be measured against the baseline, but does not define what constitutes a successful outcome (e.g., MAE improvement ≥ X eV or statistical significance).
SC-002 describes measuring predictive contribution via relative MAE increase and p‑value, yet provides no decision rule (e.g., p < 0.05 and MAE increase ≥ Y eV) to determine success.
SC-004 requires reporting the test‑train MAE gap but does not specify an acceptable maximum gap or any criterion for judging generalization adequacy.

SC-007 calls for reporting the Pearson correlation between absolute error and molecular size/flexibility, but does not define a target range or significance threshold to assess whether the correlation is acceptable.
SC-008 mandates a sensitivity analysis over a set of thresholds and reporting variation in success rates, yet it does not state what variation is acceptable (e.g., stability within ±5 %).

SC-009 measures statistical power of the ablation study via p‑values and effect‑size distribution but does not declare a minimum power (e.g., ≥ 0.8) or a maximum acceptable p‑value beyond the paired‑test criterion already in FR‑007.
SC-011 reports the count of OOD‑flagged molecules but provides no quantitative benchmark (e.g., ≤ X % of test set) to evaluate whether the OOD rate is acceptable for the study’s conclusions.
